title: Power-Ups: Double Points, Slow-Mo, Shrink
content:
## Overview
The game includes a collectible power-up system offering temporary boosts or twists during a run, layered on top of ordinary food. Three power-up types exist:

- **Double Points** -- doubles score gains for the collecting snake for a set duration.
- **Slow-Mo** -- stretches the game's tick speed for a duration. Since there is only one shared tick timer driving the board, this affects the *entire* shared game loop, including in bot-vs-bot matches with two snakes, even though only one snake collected it.
- **Shrink** -- instantly trims several tail segments off the collecting snake.

Double Points and Shrink are per-snake effects (only apply to whichever snake grabbed them), while Slow-Mo is effectively global because it modifies the shared clock.

## Availability
Power-ups only appear in **single-player** and **bot-vs-bot** modes. They are excluded from **human two-player mode**, since a shared power-up pickup would create ambiguity over which player's effect applies.

## Spawning and lifecycle
After eating food, there's a chance a power-up spawns on the board. It lingers for a limited number of moves and visibly blinks as it nears expiry, then disappears if uncollected.

A URL parameter (`?powerup=type` or `?powerup=off`) forces a specific power-up type to spawn deterministically directly in the snake's path, making the feature testable without waiting on random spawn odds.

## HUD and visuals
- A status badge shows the currently active effect and its countdown.
- A pop-up toast names the pickup just collected.
- Each power-up type has distinct color-coded visuals on the board.

## Bot awareness
All bots (twelve total) are power-up aware via a shared scoring helper (`src/bots/power-up.ts`) rather than bespoke per-bot logic, so each bot gains awareness through a single added line without disturbing its existing tuned behavior.

- Each bot has a configurable "appetite": overall pursuit strength, per-type bonus multipliers, and an optional gating rule.
- The pursuit bonus is hard-capped well below each bot's self-preservation thresholds, so no bot will ever choose a power-up over avoiding a fatal self-trap.
- Scoring is distance- and lifetime-aware: the shared bot data types and position-analysis routine (used both in the main game and the menu demo) compute the shortest path from a candidate move to the power-up, so bots discount or ignore pickups that are unreachable or likely to expire before they can arrive.

Examples of per-bot tuning:
- The aggressive Chaser bot favors Double Points and Slow-Mo.
- The tightly-coiling Coiler bot strongly favors Shrink.
- The ambush bot only strikes for pickups within its lurking range.
- The survival-focused bot never diverts if doing so would strand it.
- Perimeter/zigzag/spiral bots only take detours that fit their natural movement pattern.

## Key files
- `src/main.ts` -- power-up spawn/lifecycle, HUD, URL override, bot integration
- `src/game-types.ts` -- power-up type definitions
- `index.html`, `src/style.css` -- HUD elements and per-type visuals
- `src/bots/power-up.ts` -- shared scoring helper
- `src/bots/bot-types.ts` -- shared bot data types extended for power-up reachability
- `src/bots/chaser-bot.ts`, `src/bots/coiler-bot.ts` -- example per-bot appetite tuning
